## The prohibitions, at the length they bite

1. **The line in the ground may not be measured, dug, counted, probed, resolved, or had a rod put in it, and it may not be connected to the chapel, to the boards under the chapel, to the two holes nine feet apart, or to anything else. And the man of about fifty-two who digs may not put a rod in a third hole, may not clear or measure either of the two holes nine feet apart, and may not touch the line.** In Chapter 0339 he says yes in a room and **his condition is his and it is that he will look at it from the end of it and not put his hands on it**, and the chapter has to survive that.
2. **The woman of about fifty at the shut gate may not be asked anything, by anybody, including the protagonist, and no chapter may send anybody to her for any reason.**
3. **A notice goes to a place and not to a house, and a notice goes in a hand, unsigned, with no name at the top of it, and no chapter may put one there and no household may be rescued by a page.** **A hand is not a page, a hand stays in the hand that made it until that person dies, and the price of no name at the top of it is that nobody can do anything for you.** A question in your own words is worth more than a question in anybody else's and the reason is nine years old and it is the carrier's, not the asker's.
4. **The four days of notice is the instrument. Four of the volume's five notices are on a page, in Chapters 0326, 0327, 0328 and 0329, and the fifth is on day 335 for a room on day 339, and it is four days.** A notice on any other day is a three-day instrument and a three-day instrument does not fail, it arrives warm.
5. **A weekday is a figure and day 1 is a Tuesday and no chapter may take a weekday from a neighbouring chapter, from the table above, from a card, or from a state file — and no chapter may use an ordinal for a month.**
6. **An elapsed count is this chapter's own day number subtracted from the day the thing happened, and the day a thing happened has to be opened in a file and not remembered, and a derived value may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth.**
7. **The Crown's schedule is on a page in this volume and is standing and correct and is never opened, never filled in, never withdrawn, and never the subject of a chapter. The sheet the man of about forty-one in a very good coat will not turn over is not the schedule.**
8. **Nobody in this batch gets stronger. Adrian is Stage 2. He performs no working, no threshold is opened, the Narrow Mark is not opened a third time, the other world is not named once, nobody offers him a workway and he asks for none, and the words *passage* and *privilege* are at zero across the ten chapters and are not the words to reach for.**

## The ten days, and what each one has to carry

**These are the beats the volume outline put on the day map at §14.3. They are constraints and not a plan for the prose, and a writer who cannot make a beat work in a room with a date on the door has a worse day than a writer who moves a beat, provided the day, the weekday, the month day, the fifth notice and the prohibitions hold.**

1. **0331, day 331, a Wednesday, the sixteenth. The second of the four is in a room.** A man of about twenty-five, **a return and not an introduction, on a page in Chapter 0309**, with a second handle invented in Chapter 0327: **his left boot, mended at the front with a length of cord that is not new.** Political or procedural. **Tamsin Quill is in this chapter and the register-keeper is not, and the room is a room she is in and the other woman of twenty-nine is not.** He said in Chapter 0327 that he wrote something and is not going to say what it is and is not going to be asked, and that if he says it in a room then it is in there on the day of the room when he is not able to look at it. **He may be asked nothing and nobody may ask him whether it will go.**
2. **0332, day 332, a Thursday, the seventeenth. The third of the four is in a room.** A man of about forty-eight, on a page since Chapter 0328, with a folding knife with a hinge that has gone stiff. Political or procedural, a notice going to a room four days old, and a woman of about thirty-three who has a question about the order of nineteen stones is available and is on a page. **Nobody asks him whether it will go and nobody asks him anything he did not offer.**
3. **0333, day 333, a Friday, the eighteenth. The fourth, who has already said no.** A woman of about sixty-one with a stick of hazel she carries and does not lean on. **Character, and not about a form, and this is the chapter the volume's plan gives a *no* to and the no was already said on the fourteenth in a different room and is not said again.** The room on the eighteenth happens or it does not, and **either of those is the answer and neither of them is a failure**, and a refusal nobody asked for is the cheapest kind there is and is the only kind in this flood that nobody can take back. **No chapter may soften the no, argue with it, apologise for it or overturn it, and no chapter may make it a defeat.**
4. **0334, day 334, a Saturday, the nineteenth. Cost and consequence.** The man of about fifty-seven, who lost a season on the ninth of the Bare Month and a certainty and had both entered, and **Jonah Pike, who is on a page six times in Volume 06, serious, right about nine parts in ten, not a villain, not defeated, not leaving.** **In neither of the two chapters in this batch is anybody wrong, and the man of about fifty-seven is right about most of what he says and is not going to be argued out of it.** The case is shut, the schedule is not filled in, the Regent is nine hundred miles away, and the road north of the Marches is shut and does not open in this flood.
5. **0335, day 335, a Sunday, the twentieth. THE FIFTH NOTICE GOES OUT, FOUR DAYS, FOR A ROOM ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH, AND IT NAMES ITS MORNING INSIDE THIS CHAPTER.** A chapter about four days of a man knowing he is going to be asked, **in which there is no form at all.** **A notice goes in a hand and not in a mouth, a hand is not a page, all five of this volume's sheets are unsigned, and no name goes at the top of any of them. A question in your own words is worth more than a question in anybody else's and the reason is nine years old and it is the carrier's, not the asker's.** **Nobody is sent and nobody asks the man whether it will go, and a chapter that asks him has spent a thing the volume was built not to spend.**
6. **0336, day 336, a Monday, the twenty-first. Recovery.** Tamsin Quill with the fold, and **the man of about twenty-seven, who washes the store's board and has said out loud that he has decided not to wash the wall above it, and whose board has not been written on since day 225 and whose figures are the figures of the two hundred and twenty-fourth.** **The board is not written on in this chapter and the wall above it is not washed in it.** The consent fracture is visible in this chapter and is not mended in it and nobody apologises in it.
7. **0337, day 337, a Tuesday, the twenty-second. Cost and consequence.** The man of about fifty-seven, second of his two chapters in this batch, and what a season and a certainty cost a man who is right. **Nobody tells him he is wrong, he does not leave, and the money is still in his hand.**
8. **0338, day 338, a Wednesday, the twenty-third. Action, physical work.** **The man of about thirty-six who holds gates on a turn, with a bar stood against a post, a barrow, a spade, and a bootful emptied before he answers**, and a boy of about eleven with a yoke and two pails on the same road, **who has been saying the day out loud at that gate since the fourth day of the Bare Month and who the man of about thirty-six taught it to, and who said it back.** **Physical work in weather, and this chapter states the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph. A keeper is not a holder, the word *holder* is not defined, and the two rolls of the same gates are not put side by side and nobody may say what the difference is worth.**
9. **0339, day 339, a Thursday, the twenty-fourth. The digger's room.** **Nev Cutler, a man of about fifty-two who digs, eleven miles the other way, is in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, and he says yes, and his condition is his and it is that he will look at it from the end of it and not put his hands on it.** **He puts no rod in anything, he does not clear or measure the two holes nine feet apart, and he does not touch the line, and the chapter has to survive all three and still be a room in which a man says yes.** **A decision, counted under decision and not under political.**
10. **0340, day 340, a Friday, the twenty-fifth. THE VOLUME'S ONE PANEL.** Plain, in its own short block, with its own line breaks, no emphasis marks, and the rule at the head of this prompt. **Refused out loud in about four seconds by the man of about thirty-seven who trades on the Open Hand board, whose second handle is a board, and what it costs him is specific: the board he keeps has had a name off it once, in his own hand, in about the ninth year of this flood, and he has never said so to anybody, and the refusal is what makes him say so in the same room, and saying so is the cost.** **Put the panel in Chapter 0340 and in no other chapter, and put it in a chapter that is about a person and not about a figure, and do not let it answer anything.**

## The prose this batch is written under

1. **A chapter may not open by summarising itself, and least of all its ending.** The opening sentence states a pressure or an arrival. It does not state the finding, and the finding is the thing the chapter is for.
2. **The recapping ledger paragraph is gone and it is not coming back in another shape. No lead paragraph of this batch carries an interval figure.**
3. **A bolded speech is the only speaker marker in this manuscript.** Within a section the bold marks one voice and the two voices alternate, and a speech may not carry two speakers in one exchange. **Bold the whole of a turn or none of it. A paragraph with a plain quotation mark at the front and a bolded quotation mark in the middle is a fault and not a style**, and Batch 0002 wrote seven chapters of it and had to move quoted material into narration to fix the measure.
4. **The measure is the share of a chapter's words inside bold marks and not marks per speech.** Volume 01 is the model at 10.4 per cent and about 35 is the ceiling. **Batch 0002 opened at a mean of 25.6 per cent with four chapters above Volume 06's highest and one above the ceiling, and repaired all seven in the writing pass by narration and never by a cut speech, and finished at 7.7 to 20.8 with a mean of 15.2 in seventy-three spans. Batch 0003 opened lower still, finished at 7.0 to 18.4 with a mean of 13.4 in fifty spans, and its longest bolded turn is ninety, in Chapter 0329, and about 90 is the working ceiling and ninety-five is the hard one. Open below 18 and check it, because a batch that writes its own measurements instead of running them publishes four wrong figures in the same run as the prose.**
5. **No chapter may contain more than two consecutive exchanges between the same two people**, which is four speech paragraphs. **Batch 0002 had three runs over the ceiling, in Chapters 0313, 0316 and 0318, and broke all three with a narration beat. Batch 0003 had four chapters at the ceiling and none over it.** Every card names a third party, a task or a thing carried, and **the chapter's first paragraph has somebody's hands on something** — Batch 0003 ran ten for ten on that, and the three physical-work chapters of this batch (0327 is Batch 0003's; 0335 and 0338 are this batch's) state the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph.
6. **The counting device, the *about N seconds* refrain, the *a person who does not want to be asked* refrain and the *in about nine seconds* refrain are declared motifs of this manuscript, none of them may stand twice in one chapter, and none of them may stand in a chapter whose finding is a refusal.** **THE CHORUS FRAME — *about four people in* — IS THE ONE THAT IS OVER THE LINE, AND IT IS A FINDING AND NOT A TARGET.** Batch 0003 measured **one hundred and forty-four in two hundred and eighty-eight paragraphs on its ten files, one in two, against one in about three in Batch 0002, one in about five in Batch 0001 and one in about four across Volume 06.** The cause is named in `bible/power-system.md` §43 item 23: two of Batch 0003's chapters are rooms in which nobody is being asked anything, and the narrator's one counting habit has nothing else to attach itself to. **Batch 0004 has three rooms in which people are not being asked anything and one chapter whose subject is a man saying yes, so the frame is the first thing to watch and the measure is in the seven checks with the definition beside it. A count is not a target and the volume's cards set none; the figure is published because the figure nobody has read is not a measurement.**
7. **The people who carry the volume get a second handle beside the age and the trade and never instead of it**, and the age-and-trade form is not abolished. The handles already on a page and the same in every chapter their person is in: **the man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall and wrote the ninth line has a piece of chalk he does not use**; the woman of about fifty at the shut gate has **a brass key on a tarred cord in the apron pocket, a bar of ash in two brackets, a wooden hook, a piece of chalk, and a date in chalk on the post every morning with nothing rubbed out**; the man of about thirty-eight with the barrow has **a barrow**; the man of about thirty-four at the wharf has **a tally-board**; the man of about thirty-seven who trades on the Open Hand board has **a board**; the man of about fifty-seven has **a length of new rope he has not used**; the woman of about sixty-nine has **a tin**; Tamsin Quill has **a folded sheet of road with about nine places on it, folded the same way every time**; Hettis Roke has **a waxed slate in a case**; the man of about forty-one in a very good coat has **a hand inside a coat with nothing in it**; the man of about thirty-six who holds gates on a turn has **a bar stood against a post, a barrow, a spade, and a bootful emptied before he answers**; the girl of seventeen has **a plain slate, a lump of chalk and a cloth**; Sera Vail has **a date she has to write**. **Invented in Batch 0003 and to be carried unchanged: the man of about fifty-two who digs has a rod he does not carry; the woman of about twenty-one has a pen with the nib ground narrow, cut down with a knife; the man of about twenty-five has a left boot mended at the front with a length of cord that is not new; the man of about forty-eight has a folding knife with a hinge that has gone stiff and does not spring; the woman of about sixty-one has a stick of hazel she carries and does not lean on.**
8. **And the one that is not a style instruction. Nobody gets stronger.**

## The checks, and the definitions, and the figures that reproduce

**Publish the definition or publish nothing, and run all seven and not six.** The seven and their definitions are at `outline/volume-07.md` §20. **Run the word-run check and the banned-string list across the whole of Volume 07's thirty files written so far and not inside this batch's ten.**

**Batch 0003's own figures, with the definitions beside them, and a later writer who is handed a smaller number will believe the smaller number.** The bolded share of words, measured on the ten files with the heading line included, `---` rules counted and bold marks counted as nothing: **7.0 to 18.4 per cent, a mean of 13.4, in fifty spans**, against Volume 06's 6.2 to 21.8 with a mean of 13.8, Volume 01's 10.4 as the model and about 35 as the ceiling, and **the longest bolded turn in that batch is ninety, in Chapter 0329, and about 90 is the working ceiling and ninety-five is the hard one.** Long sentences of forty words or more: **230** across Batch 0003's ten on the definition at `state/batch-summaries/volume-06-batch-0004.md` §8.5.1, none duplicated inside a file and none across the ten. Twenty-one weekday tokens stand across those ten files and all twenty-one are correct. The word-run across Batch 0003's ten files, each file's lead paragraph subtracted: a top of **twenty-four consecutive words** between Chapters 0321 and 0324, and it is the room-lead frame, **a motif and not a duplication**, against eighty-seven between Chapters 0299 and 0300 in Volume 06 and twenty-four in Batch 0001, which is the same figure and the same class of thing. The chorus frame, on the bare head every occurrence of *about four people in*: **one hundred and forty-five in two hundred and eighty-nine paragraphs, one in two**, and it is the one figure in that batch above the house range, and **a count is not a target.** The exchange: **forty-eight plain speeches and twenty-four of them answered, fifty per cent**, and **the denominator is forty-eight and that is the whole of the caveat**, against Volume 06's 316 of 798 at thirty-nine point six and Batch 0002's 23 of 24.

**AND ONE FAULT THAT BATCH 0003 MADE IN ITS OWN WRITING PASS, WHICH A LATER WRITER WHO EDITS PROSE WITH A SCRIPT WILL RECOGNISE AND WHICH IS RECORDED IN FULL AT `state/batch-summaries/volume-07-batch-0003.md` §10 AND `state/open-threads.md` §5.** Thirty-two sites in ten chapters had a clause left abutting the clause in front of it, with a comma, a conjunction and a narrator's frame gone, after a script was run against a copy of the files that was not the copy the pass believed it was and a restore step failed silently on a directory name. All thirty-two were repaired by putting the frame back word for word and the ten files carry zero fused words. **The rule for this run: a writing pass that edits prose with a script must make its own copy first, must verify the copy it is editing against the file it means to be editing, must treat a failed copy step as a hard failure and not as a no-op, and must check for fused words afterwards on a vocabulary built from the files the pass is not touching, because a check that counts words cannot see one.**

**AND THE FIGURES A LATER WRITER WILL QUOTE FROM THE TEN CHAPTERS THIS BATCH WRITES ARE NOT YET ON A PAGE, AND THE RULE IS THE OLD ONE: a value at a chapter boundary is derived and may be used in a chapter that dates it and may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth unless a page carries it.**

`state/current.md`, `state/continuity.md`, `state/open-threads.md` and `state/character-state.md` all name `workspace/volume-07/batch-0004/PROMPT.md` now and must all name `workspace/volume-07/batch-0005/PROMPT.md` when this run finishes, **and a later phase reads `state/volume-06-close.md` first and then the newest block in each of the four, and the two must not disagree.** `bible/power-system.md` gains the next free numbered section for the ten days this batch puts on a page, **which is §44, and it does not change §32, does not change §33, and does not change §33A.** `state/chapter-summaries.md` gains ten entries and `state/batch-summaries/volume-07-batch-0004.md` is written.

**AND TWO OPEN FIGURES THIS RUN MUST RECORD IN THE STATE LAYER AS QUESTIONS AND NOT SETTLE.** The age of the man who trades on the Open Hand board, which is about thirty-seven in the outline and about thirty-nine in the prose of Volume 06. And the fact that the fourth of the four said no on the fourteenth of the Bare Month in a room with a date on the door, and that the room on the eighteenth is on the nineteenth day of this batch's range and is not a defeat and is not to be softened. **A batch that settles either of them in prose has decided something a batch may not decide.**

## What is not answered by being planned

**The boundary is not settled in this volume. The line in the orchard is not measured and not dug, and by the volume's last page it has no name at all. The ninth line does not work and nobody may say whether it does. The schedule stands and the case is shut and the Regent is nine hundred miles away and is not defeated. The board has not been written on since day 225. The man who bought half a holding loses a season and a certainty and is right. The form has a notary's name on it and no number under the first line and one man four hundred miles off is going to have to write one in himself. A man of about fifty-two who digs has a name and a rod he does not carry and a room on the twenty-fourth of the Bare Month. A man of about thirty-seven who trades on the Open Hand board has a board with a name off it that he has never mentioned. And a woman of about twenty-one is in a room and does not know what she is for, and nobody in this volume is going to tell her, and that is the last thing this batch inherits and not the first.**
